metadata.description: Fab Shuffle, running as a single-replica Azure Container App. Fab Shuffle keeps its session and run state in memory, so the app is deliberately pinned to one replica: a second one would not see your sign-in or your migration.
Optional. Leave blank to generate a stable fab-shuffle name for this resource group. To update an existing deployment, use its current app name (or leave blank if it used the generated default).
Optional Azure region code, such as canadacentral. Leave blank to use the selected resource group's region. This is where Fab Shuffle runs, not the migration's destination capacity region.
Image to run. The default is the public build from this repository and needs no registry credentials.
vCPU. Schema transfer shells out to sqlpackage, a .NET process of a few hundred megabytes, and two of those run at once by default, so 2 is the sensible floor.
Memory in GiB. Must be exactly double the vCPU count for the consumption workload profile.
Directory (tenant) GUID of the existing single-tenant Entra WEB app registration used for operator sign-in. This is separate from the Fabric runtime service principal or managed identity.

Application (client) GUID of that existing Entra WEB registration. Before deployment, enable ID tokens for hybrid sign-in and set its Application ID URI to api://<client-id>. After deployment, add the exact easyAuthCallbackUrl output as a Web redirect URI.

Required client secret VALUE for the Entra WEB registration, not its secret ID or a Fabric runtime credential. Stored only as a Container Apps secret for EasyAuth hybrid flow. Rotate before expiration.

Required nonempty array of individual operator USER object-ID GUIDs in easyAuthTenantId. No group IDs, application/client IDs, wildcard or tenant-wide default. EasyAuth and the application both enforce this allowlist.

Optional full resource ID of an EXISTING user-assigned managed identity. Leave blank to keep runtime service-principal sign-in. Use the same stable identity for the controller and scheduled sync job; grant Fabric/SQL/OneLake and capacity permissions separately.

Total Azure Files share quota in GiB, including concurrent staging and retained journals. Default 100 GiB is not a measured requirement. Use scripts/Get-FabShuffleStorageEstimate.ps1 to estimate your workload; this quota is separate from the per-operation disk and memory budgets.

Disk budget per bounded schema/checkpoint operation, in GiB. Does not reserve space or resize the Azure Files share. Legacy single-principal AzCopy/bcp exports are not capped by this setting; size the share for their full staging requirements.

In-memory transfer/metadata budget per operation, in MiB. This is not the container RAM limit or a hard process cap. Leave room for concurrent workers, Python and external tools; increasing disk staging does not require increasing this budget.

Persistent SMB storage authenticated with an account key. Large file shares are explicitly enabled because the shares API still documents that gate for quotas above 5120 GiB, even though newer guidance calls it a legacy setting. EasyAuth protects the wizard, not this authenticated public storage endpoint; see README for private-network requirements and key rotation.

Private coordination container only. The runtime conditionally creates one empty lease blob; recovery metadata remains in the central Warehouse. Do not remove or change this lock while a controller operation is running.

resources.name: [guid(resourceId('Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/containers', variables('storageAccountName'), 'default', variables('bcdrLeaseContainerName')), parameters('managedIdentityResourceId'), 'Storage Blob Data Contributor')]

metadata.description: Storage Blob Data Contributor at the dedicated lock CONTAINER only, never the storage account, resource group or subscription. The deployer needs roleAssignments/write here. Does not authorize Fabric, SQL, OneLake or capacity power management.

EXTERNAL wizard URL after final activation, built from Azure's reported environment domain. Deployment remains internal and application-ready=false. Verify auth, enable ingress while still not ready, read the actual FQDN/register its callback, then activate the application LAST.

The external hostname's callback, not the temporary .internal. hostname. Add this exact URI to the EXISTING single-tenant Entra application's Web redirect URIs; verify the reported FQDN after enabling ingress. ARM does not create or update that registration.

verifyAuthenticationCommand.value: [format('az containerapp auth show --subscription "{0}" --resource-group "{1}" --name "{2}" --output json', subscription().subscriptionId, resourceGroup().name, variables('appName'))]

metadata.description: FIRST inspect the deployed auth config: enabled platform/AAD, RedirectToLoginPage, tenant-v2 issuer, app audiences, nonempty exact operator identities, only /api/health excluded, and fab-shuffle-easyauth secret reference. Do not activate if deployment/auth validation failed.

activateApplicationCommand.value: [format('az containerapp update --subscription "{0}" --resource-group "{1}" --name "{2}" --set-env-vars FAB_SHUFFLE_EASYAUTH_READY=true --only-show-errors --output none', subscription().subscriptionId, resourceGroup().name, variables('appName'))]

metadata.description: LAST, only after successful deployment, auth verification, ingress enablement, actual-FQDN verification and Web callback registration. Sets only readiness and creates a new revision. Wait for completion, then verify allowed/disallowed sign-ins. Other env, mounts, image and identity are not replaced.

enablePublicIngressCommand.value: [format('az containerapp ingress enable --subscription "{0}" --resource-group "{1}" --name "{2}" --type external --target-port 8080 --transport auto --only-show-errors --output none', subscription().subscriptionId, resourceGroup().name, variables('appName'))]

metadata.description: AFTER successful deployment and verifyAuthenticationCommand, WHILE application-ready=false. Enables external HTTPS ingress without replacing the app template. Then readPublicFqdnCommand, configure callback, and activateApplicationCommand LAST. Every ARM redeploy closes ingress and resets readiness.

readPublicFqdnCommand.value: [format('az containerapp show --subscription "{0}" --resource-group "{1}" --name "{2}" --query properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn --output tsv', subscription().subscriptionId, resourceGroup().name, variables('appName'))]

metadata.description: After enabling ingress while application-ready=false, read the actual external hostname. Add https://<this-fqdn>/.auth/login/aad/callback as the registration's Web redirect URI; it must agree with easyAuthCallbackUrl. Only then activate the application.
Reuse this environment in the scheduled-sync job deployment, in this same resource group and location.

Reuse this EXACT non-secret lease URL in the scheduled job. OAuth only; never add a SAS. An SP-mode BCDR controller also needs Storage Blob Data Contributor on bcdrLeaseContainerResourceId, granted separately.
Object ID for explicit Fabric and Azure role grants. Attaching the identity grants no Fabric, SQL, OneLake or Azure capacity permissions.
